newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks seen moving higher, eyes on red chips.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks seen moving higher, eyes on red chips.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to move higher on Monday after the Dow industrials closed at a record high on Friday, with the focus on red-chip stocks ahead of the listing this week of Beijing Enterprises.

"Interest will continue to be focused on red chips today and futures-related buying is also expected on individual big cap stocks," said Peter Lui, in institutional sales at NAVA SC Securities. But he said intra-day profit-taking could cap gains.
The Hang Seng Index rose 119.68 points to a record close of 14,331.68 on Friday. Later, the Hang Seng London Reference Index eased 9.26 points to 14,322.42.
Charles Cheung, executive director at J & A Securities said market sentiment was further boosted by the excitment over the initial public offering of Beijing Enterprises Holdings Ltd.
"The market is overbought and many of the red chips have risen more than 10 percent," Cheung said.
Light profit-taking on individaul red chips might set in but a price adjustment was unlikely until Thursday when Beijing Enterprises shares start trading.
Brokers said interest was seen in blue-chip property stocks ahead of next week's government land auction.
